correctness.rationale: Every binary term has coefficient a in R=F_p[T]. Closure under right translations in the finite coefficient quandle, including rho_0 and rho_I, forces S=R: their conjugates yield all translations T^j(I-T), whose additive span is R since I-T is a unit. Arbitrary equations reduce to linear maps with image equal to g(T)V for a divisor g of the minimal polynomial; each such image is realized by a two-variable equation. Primary cyclic-module kernel dimensions give the boxed spectrum for all n; irreducible minimal polynomial is exactly the no-intermediate-kernel condition. Eight concrete Latin matrix cases were checked by standalone coefficient-closure, matrix rank and direct solution-count computations.

value.rationale: The result completely calculates a newly studied, natural equational invariant over the entire class of finite Latin affine quandles with elementary abelian underlying group and identifies the sharp minimal-spectrum locus in module-theoretic terms. It resolves a genuine distinction: a nonsimple scalar-action quandle can have minimal spectrum, so known simplicity classification does not replace the finding. It handles semisimple, mixed-primary and nonsemisimple matrices uniformly and identifies all intermediate levels by elementary divisors.
